Using Python with Pillow (PIL), read /in/sales.csv and draw a bar chart of sales per month into /out/sales.png, exactly 640x400 pixels, white background, one bar per month with the month name written under each bar. Then, with a second Python command, open the PNG and print its size and mode.
I'll help you create a bar chart from the CSV data and then verify the PNG file. Let me start by examining the CSV file to understand its structure.
Now I'll create a Python script to read this CSV and generate the bar chart with the specified requirements:

input.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import csv
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

# Read the CSV file
with open('/in/sales.csv', 'r') as f:
    reader = csv.DictReader(f)
    data = [(row['month'], int(row['sales'])) for row in reader]

# Create image with white background, exactly 640x400 pixels
width, height = 640, 400
img = Image.new('RGB', (width, height), 'white')
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Calculate bar dimensions
num_bars = len(data)
margin = 40
chart_height = height - 80  # Leave space for labels at bottom
bar_width = (width - 2 * margin) // num_bars - 10
spacing = (width - 2 * margin) // num_bars

# Find max sales for scaling
max_sales = max(sales for _, sales in data)

# Draw bars
for i, (month, sales) in enumerate(data):
    # Calculate bar height proportional to sales
    bar_height = int((sales / max_sales) * chart_height)
    
    # Calculate bar position
    x = margin + i * spacing + 5
    y = height - 60 - bar_height  # 60px from bottom for labels
    
    # Draw bar
    draw.rectangle([x, y, x + bar_width, height - 60], fill='blue')
    
    # Draw month label below bar
    text = month
    # Calculate text position to center it under the bar
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text)
    text_width = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    text_x = x + (bar_width - text_width) // 2
    text_y = height - 40
    draw.text((text_x, text_y), text, fill='black')
    
    # Draw sales value on top of bar
    sales_text = str(sales)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), sales_text)
    sales_width = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    sales_x = x + (bar_width - sales_width) // 2
    sales_y = y - 20
    draw.text((sales_x, sales_y), sales_text, fill='black')

# Save the image
img.save('/out/sales.png')
print("Chart created successfully at /out/sales.png")
EOF

width, height = 640, 400
img = Image.new('RGB', (width, height), 'white')
draw = ImageDraw.Draw(img)

# Calculate bar dimensions
num_bars = len(data)
margin = 40
chart_height = height - 80  # Leave space for labels at bottom
bar_width = (width - 2 * margin) // num_bars - 10
spacing = (width - 2 * margin) // num_bars

# Find max sales for scaling
max_sales = max(sales for _, sales in data)

# Draw bars
for i, (month, sales) in enumerate(data):
    # Calculate bar height proportional to sales
    bar_height = int((sales / max_sales) * chart_height)
    
    # Calculate bar position
    x = margin + i * spacing + 5
    y = height - 60 - bar_height  # 60px from bottom for labels
    
    # Draw bar
    draw.rectangle([x, y, x + bar_width, height - 60], fill='blue')
    
    # Draw month label below bar
    text = month
    # Calculate text position to center it under the bar
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), text)
    text_width = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    text_x = x + (bar_width - text_width) // 2
    text_y = height - 40
    draw.text((text_x, text_y), text, fill='black')
    
    # Draw sales value on top of bar
    sales_text = str(sales)
    bbox = draw.textbbox((0, 0), sales_text)
    sales_width = bbox[2] - bbox[0]
    sales_x = x + (bar_width - sales_width) // 2
    sales_y = y - 20
    draw.text((sales_x, sales_y), sales_text, fill='black')

# Save the image
img.save('/out/sales.png')
print("Chart created successfully at /out/sales.png")
EOF
